name: bundlephobia
description: Bundlephobia shows the bundle-size cost of npm packages. This CLI searches packages and looks up minified/gzipped size, dependency composition, version history, similar packages, exports, recent searches and download/star trends. It can also fetch a GitHub repo's package.json to scan its dependencies.

commands.name: search-packages
commands.summary: Autocomplete/search npm package names (npms.io suggestions used by the Bundlephobia search box)

params.name: q
params.description: Search text or package-name prefix; scopes allowed, e.g. '@grida'

commands.name: get-package-size
commands.summary: Get minified and gzipped bundle size, dependency count and module flags for an npm package (optionally a specific version)

params.name: package
params.description: Package name, optionally with a version: 'react', 'react@19.3.1', '@mui/material'

commands.name: get-package-history
commands.summary: List a package's recent versions with their bundle sizes and publish dates, plus major/minor release markers

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Maximum number of versions to return (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: get-similar-packages
commands.summary: Find alternative or similar packages in the same category as a given package

commands.name: list-recent-searches
commands.summary: List packages recently searched on Bundlephobia by all users, keyed by package name

params.name: api_limit
params.description: Number of recent packages to return (sent to the site as "limit"; clify's own --limit only shapes the output)

commands.name: compare-trends
commands.summary: Compare download, star and size trends over time for several packages (the data behind the /trends page)

commands.name: get-github-package-json
commands.summary: Fetch the package.json of a GitHub repo (default branch) to list its dependencies for scanning with get-package-size

notes: The Bundlephobia API rate-limits aggressively (HTTP 429), especially trends, history, exports and similar-packages. Space out calls and retry with backoff; do not bulk-scan many packages quickly.
Package arguments accept 'name', 'name@version' and scoped names like '@scope/name'. Without a version, the latest version is used.
get-package-size records the lookup in the public 'recent searches' list (record=true), the same as the website does.
get-package-details reads __NEXT_DATA__ from the package page. On first load of a package not yet built, initialResult may be null; if so, call get-package-size instead.

The response shapes of get-package-exports and compare-trends were only partly captured because of rate limiting. The trends UI also offers metric=downloads|stars|size and groupBy=day|week|month, but those are client-side display options.
Scan workflow: run get-github-package-json, then call get-package-size for each dependency name.
Bundlephobia also exposes an MCP endpoint at https://bundlephobia.com/api/mcp.
